prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” personal injury attorney for every Chicago car-accident claim — the right lawyer depends on your case facts, how serious your injuries are, whether fault is disputed, whether the other driver is uninsured, and how much trial experience you want. Instead of one name, choose an attorney or firm that fits these criteria:

What to look for
- Substantial experience handling car-accident claims (not just brief intake work).  
- Trial experience and a record of substantial settlements/verdicts in similar cases.  
- Good reputation: peer reviews (Martindale‑Hubbell), Super Lawyers listings, Best Lawyers, or similar.  
- Client reviews and references.  
- Resources to investigate and litigate (experts, accident reconstruction, medical liens).  
- Clear contingency-fee agreement (no recovery, no fee except costs) and transparent fee/cost policy.  
- Strong communication: who will handle your case day-to-day, how you’ll be updated, response time.  
- Willingness to take cases to trial if needed (not all firms settle quickly).  

Where to search / verify
- Chicago Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service.  
- Illinois State Bar Association referral.  
- Online directories: Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, Avvo (read reviews carefully).  
- Ask friends/family or other attorneys for referrals.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled? What were typical outcomes?  
- Will you personally handle my case or will associates/paralegals?  
- Do you have trial experience in car-accident cases? Have you gone to verdict?  
- How do you charge (contingency fee %)? What costs could I owe if we lose?  
- What’s your estimated timeline and likely strategy for my case?  
- Who are your typical experts (medical, accident reconstruction)?  
- Can you provide client references or recent settlements/verdicts for similar cases?

Practical items to bring to consultations
- Police report, photos/video of the crash and damage, traffic camera links if any.  
- Medical records, bills, and a summary of injuries/symptoms and treatments.  
- Insurance info (yours and other parties’), correspondence from insurers.  
- Names/contact info for witnesses.  
- Pay stubs or documentation of time missed from work.

Timing and deadlines
- In Illinois, the general statute of limitations for personal injury is two years from the date of the accident (some exceptions apply). Don’t delay contacting an attorney.

- Power Rogers & Smith
